Education Minister and Tamale South MP, Haruna Iddrisu, says Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has performed better in managing Ghana's economy than his predecessor, Ken Ofori-Atta.
He argued that improvements in key economic indicators, Ghana's exit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme and upgrades in the country's credit ratings demonstrate the difference in economic management under the two ministers.
Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Iddrisu said the comparison between the two finance ministers should be settled in favour of Dr Ato Forson.
“Mr. Speaker, the debate is ongoing there between former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta at the time versus Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, Finance Minister today. Mr. Speaker, let it be settled. And indeed, it is a settled debate that Dr Ato Forson wins the debate when it comes to any measure or any judgment of the management of the economy,” he said.
He questioned how the current Finance Minister could have secured Ghana's exit from the IMF programme if his management of the economy was not better than that of Mr Ofori-Atta.
Mr Iddrisu also cited credit rating assessments by Standard & Poor's, Fitch and Moody's, saying the agencies had upgraded Ghana's ratings from CCC+ to B with a stable outlook.
On inflation, he said the rate declined from 23.8 per cent in 2024 to 5.5 per cent in October 2026 under Dr Ato Forson.
He compared this with the previous administration's record, noting that inflation fell from 15.4 per cent in 2016 to 9.4 per cent by the end of 2018 under Mr Ofori-Atta.
The Tamale South MP further highlighted Ghana's gross international reserves, arguing that "the country had recorded an improvement under the current Finance Minister compared with the position inherited from the previous administration."
He said the economic indicators provided sufficient evidence to support his position that Dr Ato Forson had performed better in managing the economy.
